**Comprehensive, reproducible multi-paragraph example (answering the rewritten question):**  
Studying a language effectively starts with consistent exposure and clear goals. Pick a level-appropriate resource (graded readers, beginner podcasts, or a structured course) and set a small daily target, like 20 minutes of listening plus 10 new words.

Rehearsing matters because it turns passive recognition into active skill. Use spaced repetition for vocabulary (e.g., flashcards), and do short daily speaking or writing drills. For speaking, shadow short audio clips and record yourself to compare pronunciation; for writing, keep a simple journal and revise entries after getting corrections.

To keep progress measurable, rotate activities: one day focus on listening + shadowing, the next on reading + summarizing, then on conversation practice. Every week, do a quick self-check (retell a story, write a short paragraph, or take a mini-quiz) to identify what to review next.

4) Feedback (2 min): note 1 recurring mistake to fix tomorrow

- 1 review day (no new words; only consolidate)
